definition: Imageability is a measure of how easily a physical object, word or environment will evoke a clear mental image in the mind of any person observing it.
details: It is used in architecture and city planning, in psycholinguistics, and in automated computer vision research. In automated image recognition, training models to connect images with concepts that have low imageability can lead to biased and harmful results.

explainer.lead: Imageability measures how easily an object, word or environment brings a clear mental image to mind. It matters because low-imageability concepts are harder to learn from images and can lead models toward biased or harmful results.

tiers.eli5: Some words instantly make a picture in your head, like 'dog'; others, like 'justice', are foggy — that ease is imageability.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use imageability ratings when pairing images with concepts and when auditing training sets for hard-to-visualize labels. A pitfall is training on low-imageability concepts, which can produce biased and harmful outputs.
tiers.paperLevel: Imageability is a graded measure of how readily a stimulus evokes a clear mental image, used in architecture, city planning, psycholinguistics and computer vision. Its limits are that it is a subjective rating, not a directly computable property of an image.

explainer.example: A dataset pairing photos with the concept 'chair' has high imageability, whereas pairing them with 'freedom' is low and can skew what the model learns.
